- **Business Logic:** Encapsulate all business logic within `@Service` classes.

- **Parameterized Logging:** Use parameterized messages (`logger.info("Processing user {}...", userI

content.value_statement: Spring Boot projects can become inconsistent across layers, configuration, testing, and security. This skill gives concise best-practice guidance for designing maintainable Java services with Spring Boot.
actual_capabilities: Guides Maven or Gradle setup and Spring Boot starter selection.
Recommends domain-based package structure and constructor-based dependency injection.
Explains externalized configuration, typed properties, profiles, and secret handling.
Covers REST controllers, DTO usage, validation, and global error handling.
Advises on services, transactions, repositories, logging, testing, and Spring Security.
limitations: Does not generate a complete application scaffold by itself.
Does not inspect a repository unless the user provides files or context.
Does not replace official Spring documentation for version-specific behavior.
Does not configure cloud infrastructure or deployment pipelines.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Service
use_cases.description: Use the skill to choose structure, dependencies, configuration patterns, and security defaults before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing API
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to evaluate controllers, DTOs, validation, error handling, transactions, and repository boundaries.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Use the testing guidance to select unit tests, integration tests, Spring test slices, and Testcontainers where useful.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Spring Boot Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a new Spring Boot service. Recommend package structure, build tool choices, starters, configuration files, and security defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Review a REST Layer
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer reviewing controllers and API contracts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Spring Boot REST layer. Check DTO usage, validation, endpoint design, error handling, and whether entities are exposed.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Data and Service Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Team refining service and repository design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate my Spring Boot service and data layers. Focus on transaction scope, stateless services, repository use, custom queries, and projections.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Spring Boot application for production readiness. Cover configuration, secrets, logging, testing strategy, Spring Security, and input handling.

output_examples.input: A team asks how to organize a new order service.
output: Recommend grouping code by business domain, such as orders and users.
Use Spring Boot starters for web and persistence needs.
Keep dependencies explicit with constructor injection and final fields.

output_examples.input: A developer asks why API responses expose database entities.
output: Explain the risks of exposing persistence models directly.
Recommend DTOs for request and response shapes.
Add validation and centralized error handling for consistent responses.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks how to test a controller and repository.
output: Use focused test slices for controllers and repositories.
Use full context integration tests only when behavior crosses layers.
Consider Testcontainers when tests need real databases or brokers.

best_practices: Provide the Spring Boot version, build tool, and relevant modules when asking for advice.
Ask for reviews by layer so feedback stays focused and actionable.
Include security, testing, and configuration requirements before requesting architecture guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not expose JPA entities directly through public API responses.
Do not hardcode secrets in configuration files or source code.
Do not use full application context tests when a focused test slice is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps apply Spring Boot best practices across structure, configuration, web APIs, services, data access, logging, testing, and security.

faq.question: Can it generate a full Spring Boot application?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and review prompts, but it is not a complete application generator.

faq.question: Does it support both Maven and Gradle?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance mentions Maven and Gradle as supported build tool choices.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Spring Security, strong password hashing, safe secret handling, and protection against injection and XSS.

faq.question: Is this skill specific to one Spring Boot version?
faq.answer: No. It gives general best practices, so users should verify version-specific details against official documentation.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
